summary: Built the configuration-change half of the open sweep gap and requested a fresh isolated execution for it. The sweep case in the fixed harness now proposes ConfChangeV2 events (single AddLearnerNode/AddNode/RemoveNode changes on node 4) on the current leader through confChangeToMsg/MsgProp, and - unlike the earlier revision, which only advanced raftLog.applied - the persist/apply step hands every committed EntryConfChangeV2 to applyConfChange after unmarshalling, so each node's tracked configuration actually changes. Two construction facts came out of doing it: the first draft panicked inside the repository's own network helper (raft_test.go:4117 dereferenced a missing state machine) as soon as a leader sent a message to the newly configured node 4, which shows the network helper has no state machine for an id that exists only in the configuration, and registering the package's black-hole stepper for that id makes those messages drop instead, after which the case runs. The draft-side run reports seeds=60, steps_per_seed=60, elections=467, ordinary proposals=452, conf_change_proposals=317 and violations=0, so the four invariants still show no counterexample once configuration changes are in the event set - but that is construction feedback only, so the experiment request asks for the same bytes to be executed in isolation; probes A-C are unchanged and the request records why fresh bytes were needed. Still missing from the wider event set: restarts from persisted storage (with the ConfState the harness must carry forward itself), and the liveness witness for whether the campaign guard's applied-lag condition can leave a cluster without an electable voter, so gap 984747de5ed94b4ea8f6977b2a92808f-gap-2 stays open pending that receipt and those additions.
